boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Juniata College traditions spanning surprise outings, scholarship, service, seasonal celebrations, and ceremonial life.

cards.title: Make the Case at Bailey Oratorical
cards.subtitle: Juniata’s ongoing academic tradition established in 1910
cards.notes: Attend the contest to hear students build and deliver original arguments within Juniata’s longest-running academic tradition.
cards.short_summary: A century-old speaking contest turns student arguments into a public campus event.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata identifies the Bailey Oratorical Contest as its oldest ongoing tradition of academic excellence and says the original award was established in 1910.
cards.access_notes: A recurring academic contest; consult Juniata’s event information for the current date and venue.

cards.title: Wait for Mountain Day to Be Declared
cards.subtitle: A surprise class-free outing tied to Raystown Lake
cards.notes: Listen for the announcement, then follow official transportation and activity guidance for the college-wide day at Raystown Lake.
cards.short_summary: The date stays secret until Juniata calls off classes and sends the community outdoors.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata says Mountain Day has existed since the late 1800s, its date is kept secret, classes are canceled, and the campus community heads to Raystown Lake.
cards.access_notes: Held on an unannounced date; participants should follow the college’s same-day instructions.

cards.title: Cross Disciplines at the Symposium
cards.subtitle: A full day devoted to Juniata student scholarship and creativity
cards.notes: Build a route across posters, performances, laboratories, and studios to see how different Juniata disciplines present their work.
cards.short_summary: Regular classes give way to a campus-wide showcase of student research and creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata describes its Liberal Arts Symposium as a day-long celebration and cherished academic tradition highlighting student work across research, performance, fieldwork, and art.
cards.access_notes: A scheduled campus symposium; consult the current program for presentation locations and attendance details.

cards.title: Start the Semester at Lobsterfest
cards.subtitle: Juniata’s first-week picnic and student-organization fair
cards.notes: Walk the organization displays while the opening-week picnic is underway, and note groups you may want to meet after the event.
cards.short_summary: A lobster picnic doubles as Juniata’s beginning-of-semester club showcase.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata says Lobsterfest closes the first week of fall classes with a picnic featuring Maine lobster and hosts the Student Organization Fair.
cards.access_notes: Sponsored by Campus Life and Juniata Dining; eligibility and meal access should be confirmed through current campus notices.

cards.title: Pitch a Tent for Madrigal
cards.subtitle: A November quad competition connected to table selection
cards.notes: Join only through the organized campus process, prepare for cold weather, and follow every current safety and roll-call requirement.
cards.short_summary: Tent teams compete through games and performances for preferred seating at Madrigal.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata documents Tenting as a November quad tradition in which teams earn points through activities for improved chances at preferred Madrigal tables.
cards.access_notes: A student-organized week-long November activity; follow current college rules, weather guidance, and participation instructions.

cards.title: Sing All Twelve Days at Madrigal
cards.subtitle: A faculty-served dinner ending in a campus sing-along
cards.notes: Dress for the announced format, watch the campus performances, and be ready to join your section during the closing song.
cards.short_summary: Faculty service, student performances, and one elaborately divided carol close the fall term.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata describes Madrigal as a holiday dinner served by faculty and staff, followed by campus performances and a sing-along of “The Twelve Days of Christmas.”
cards.access_notes: A seasonal dinner and dance; table selection and attendance procedures depend on current campus announcements.

cards.title: Take Juniata’s Service Day Off Campus
cards.subtitle: Volunteer projects across Huntingdon County
cards.notes: Register for an assigned project, wear task-appropriate clothing, and follow the host organization’s instructions at the service site.
cards.short_summary: The college marks Martin Luther King Jr. Day through practical work with regional organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata says its MLK Day of Service sends volunteers to direct-service projects across Huntingdon County, including libraries, community centers, schools, and animal welfare work.
cards.access_notes: Projects and sites vary; use the college’s current registration and transportation instructions.

cards.title: Take the Pre-Finals Springfest Break
cards.subtitle: Music, games, food trucks, and snow cones on the quad
cards.notes: Check the day’s activity schedule, meet friends on the quad, and use the festival as a planned break from finals preparation.
cards.short_summary: Juniata turns the quad into a spring festival as final-exam preparation approaches.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata identifies Springfest as a campus tradition held around finals preparation, with live music, games, food trucks, and snow cones on the quad.
cards.access_notes: A seasonal quad event; consult the current campus schedule for timing, vendors, and weather changes.

cards.title: Pause Before Commencement
cards.subtitle: An interfaith reflection led by members of the graduating class
cards.notes: Arrive ready to listen as graduating students share readings, poetry, personal reflections, and music before commencement.
cards.short_summary: Graduates frame their Juniata experience through an interfaith evening of reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata calls Baccalaureate one of its longest-standing traditions and describes an interfaith service featuring readings, poetry, personal sharing, and graduating-class participation.
cards.access_notes: Held on the Friday night before Commencement; verify the current ceremony location and guest arrangements.

cards.title: Watch the Centennial Mace Lead the Ceremony
cards.subtitle: A 1975 staff carried at opening convocation and commencement
cards.notes: Look for the faculty marshal and inspect the mace’s four bronze medallions, each connecting Juniata with its institutional history.
cards.short_summary: A carved ceremonial staff carries pieces of Juniata and Huntingdon history into academic processions.
cards.evidence_claim: Juniata Magazine says the Centennial Mace was crafted in 1975 and is carried by the faculty marshal at opening convocation and Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Visible during designated academic ceremonies; ceremony attendance rules and locations vary by event.
